companion.configure.what: change a node's own settings the way a phone would, sending only the fields that were asked for, and reporting which ones went

params.name: node
params.what: the connected node; refused when nothing is connected to it

params.name: name
params.what: the name the node advertises itself under; absent or empty leaves it alone

params.name: lat
params.what: latitude in degrees; absent leaves the advertised position alone, and giving it is what makes `lon` be read at all

params.name: lon
params.what: longitude in degrees, read only when `lat` was given; absent alongside a `lat` sends zero

params.name: tx_dbm
params.what: transmit power in dBm; absent leaves it alone

params.name: freq_khz
params.what: centre frequency in kHz, refused outside 150000 to 2500000; absent with another modem field given keeps what the node last said it holds

params.name: bw_khz
params.what: bandwidth in kHz, refused outside 7 to 500; absent with another modem field given keeps what the node last said it holds

params.name: sf
params.what: spreading factor, refused outside 5 to 12; absent with another modem field given keeps what the node last said it holds

params.name: cr
params.what: coding rate denominator, refused outside 5 to 8; absent with another modem field given keeps what the node last said it holds

params.name: path_hash
params.what: bytes of path hash each hop adds, 1 to 3, refused outside that; absent leaves it alone

companion.configure.answers: `set` names what was sent, in the order it went. A call that asks for nothing at all is refused rather than answered with an empty list. The four modem fields go as one command, so any one of them is refused until the node has said what its radio is.

example.what: turn a node's transmit power down
